title: Answer: a proof that the combination problem cannot be solved, or that physics needs no categorical ground

statements.text: Chalmers finds no direct evidence against the view. It would be undercut if the combination problem were proved unsolvable, if physics turned out to be structure or dispositions all the way down, or if structural truths were shown to entail all truths about experience, which would vindicate traditional physicalism.

sources.quote: Like epiphenomenalism, the view appears to be compatible with all our evidence, and there is no direct evidence against it.
If one of these problems can be solved or proved unsolvable, that will constitute significant progress on the mind–body problem.
